newsitem.title: LEBANON: Suspected Japanese Red Army members held in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Suspected Japanese Red Army members held in Beirut.

text.p: Lebanese security forces have arrested a number of Japanese citizens suspected of belonging to the Red Army guerrilla group and are interrogating them, Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said on Tuesday.

In Japan, Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said earlier on Tuesday that Lebanese authorities had arrested up to six key members of the Red Army, including a gunman involved in the 1972 Lod airport massacre in Israel.

"There are some Japanese citizens who are supposed to be members of the Japanese Red Army and who are actually with the Lebanese security forces who are interrogating (them) concerning their implication in some events," Bouez told reporters.
"The interrogation began a little time ago and we are waiting to see what are exactly their responsibilities concerning participation in any crime," Bouez, speaking in English, added.

He did not specify the number of those detained or where or when the arrests took place, but earlier official Lebanese sources said up to six Red Army members had been arrested in the Syrian-controlled Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon two days ago.

"A number of Japanese have been arrested two days ago in the Bekaa Valley. There are five or six of them and according to the Interpol arrest warrants they are members of the Japanese Red Army," an official source in Beirut told Reuters.

Hashimoto told reporters in Japan he had been informed by Lebanese officials that the ageing guerrillas and three supporters, all of them Japanese, were arrested in the Bekaa where they had been holed up for years.
According to the Lebanese officials the detainees included 49-year-old Kozo Okamoto, who was involved in the May 1972 shootout at Tel Aviv's Lod airport in which 24 people died and 100 were injured.

The Red Army, founded in 1971, is allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions. The Bekaa Valley was a haven during Lebanon's 1975-90 civil war for guerrilla groups including Lebanese Moslems and Marxists, Palestinians, Kurds and the Japanese Red Army.
There was no immediate indication whether Japan was requesting the extradition of the Red Army members.
The sources said Japanese ambassador Yasujji Ishikagi told Lebanese foreign ministry officials on Monday that a Japanese security mission had arrived in Beirut.
"The ambassador told the officials that the mission is here to help the Lebanese government in the investigations and it has information it wants to provide the authorities with," the source said.

Japanese embassy officials and members of the security mission met Lebanon's prosecutor-general Adnan Addoum in the early afternoon over the arrests. Both sides declined to comment to reporters after the meeting.
Japanese media reports have named four of the detained guerrillas as Kazuo Tohira, 44, Hisashi Matsuda, 48, Mariko Yamamoto, 56, and Masao Adachi, 57.
